When bad loans rose, was it the lender or the economy?

Ten audited years of credit risk at two large private banks, benchmarked against their peers. We test which shocks were bank-specific and which were sector-wide, and whether the share price saw it coming.

FRA Group Project 2 · Credit risk · FY2017–FY2026

When bad loans rose, was it the lender or the economy?

We studied IndusInd Bank and HDFC Bank over ten audited years. Each bank was benchmarked against a separately defined peer group: four peers for IndusInd Bank and three peers for HDFC Bank. We sorted every rise in bad loans into bank-specific (idiosyncratic) or sector-wide (systematic), then checked whether the share price noticed. Credit-risk metrics are sourced from audited annual reports. Market data and event information are sourced separately from financial market databases, regulatory disclosures and documented news sources.

Q1 · Credit risk vs peersHDFC stayed low and steady; IndusInd ran above its peers on specific NPA credit cost every year since FY2019.

FY2026 gross NPA: IndusInd 3.43% vs its 4-peer median 1.22%; HDFC 1.15% vs its 3-peer median 1.24%.

See the comparison →
Q2 · Idiosyncratic or systematic?Both. Sector-wide shocks repeatedly turned into IndusInd-specific losses because of where its loans were concentrated.

IL&FS (FY2019) and microfinance (FY2025) were systemic triggers with bank-specific amplification at IndusInd; FY2018 and COVID were systematic.

See the episodes →
Q3 · Did the share price react?Yes, fast and sometimes early, at the moment news came out. Year-end ratios barely explain annual returns.

IndusInd recorded a three-day market-model abnormal return of −8.5% following the IL&FS-related shock, compared with a peer-adjusted abnormal return of −7.0% (raw three-day stock return about −10.1%).

See the market test →
00 · Setup

Two banks, two peer groups, ten years

The brief asks for two entities, a justified peer set for each, and at least ten years of data.

IndusInd BankLarge private bank
Business
Vehicle loans, microfinance (via BFIL, merged 2019) and corporate lending
Peers
HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak
Why these peers
The other four large listed private banks: same RBI rules for bad loans and capital, full ten-year audited history. Four peers give a stable median.
HDFC BankLarge private bank
Business
Retail and wholesale; home loans added through the HDFC Ltd merger (July 2023)
Peers
ICICI, Axis, Kotak
Why these peers
Banks of comparable scale and product range. IndusInd is left out: it is about one-ninth HDFC's size, and its own crisis would distort HDFC's benchmark.

The ten-year window covers three stress periods

Stress periodStructural break (merger)

FY2018: sector-wide bad-loan clean-up after RBI audits. FY2021: COVID-19. FY2025: microfinance downturn. FY = year ending 31 March; FY2026 ends March 2026 and is audited.

02 · Question two

Bank-specific or sector-wide?

Idiosyncratic means the bank got worse while peers did not. Systematic means everyone got worse together.

Step 1Spot the jump

Flag a year when the focus bank's GNPA rose >0.20pp, slippages >0.50pp or specific NPA credit cost >0.30pp. These are screening thresholds only.

Step 2Check the peers

If most peers also worsened by a similar amount, it is systematic. If peers held steady or improved, it is idiosyncratic. Otherwise it is mixed.

Step 3Prove the cause

Confirm with annual reports, RBI circulars and the press. If no filing explains it, we say the cause is undisclosed.

Screening, not proof. The thresholds only flag years worth investigating; on their own they do not establish cause. The final classification also weighs how the peer banks moved, macroeconomic conditions (for example COVID), regulatory developments (RBI audits, circulars and moratoriums) and bank-specific evidence from annual reports and disclosures.

Where the two bars move together, the stress was shared (systematic). Where the focus bar rises alone, it was bank-specific (idiosyncratic).

What drove each kind of risk

Systematic drivers
  • RBI asset-quality audits and the Feb-2018 framework forced every bank to recognise hidden bad loans (FY2017–18).
  • IL&FS default (Sep 2018) triggered a broad liquidity shock across the NBFC and credit markets: the systemic dimension of the IL&FS episode.
  • COVID-19 (FY2021): lockdowns, a loan moratorium and a court freeze on NPA tagging.
  • RBI's Nov-2021 NPA rule (no upgrade until all arrears are paid) raised slippages and upgrades for all banks.
  • Microfinance downturn (FY2025) after borrowers became over-leveraged across the sector.
Idiosyncratic drivers
  • IndusInd: IL&FS concentration. Its exposure of about Rs 3,004 cr to the group became NPA in FY2019. This is the bank-specific amplification of a systemic shock, and the reason its GNPA rose while peers' fell.
  • IndusInd: microfinance concentration. Its microfinance book made it far more exposed to the FY2025 downturn than peers (Axis: microfinance about 1.2% of retail loans).
  • IndusInd: accounting and governance lapses (Rs 1,960 cr derivative write-off, FY2025). These hit profit and the share price, not loan quality, so we keep them separate.
  • HDFC: merger, not credit. HDFC Ltd brought Rs 12,281 cr of bad loans in FY2024. That is a structural break, not deterioration.
03 · Question three

Did the share price react, and was there a correlation?

We tested this two ways: the reaction in the days around each news event, and the relationship between yearly credit changes and yearly stock returns.

AnswerThe market reacted strongly to bank-specific news, often within a day and sometimes before the bad loans were even reported. Sector-wide shocks barely moved HDFC against its peers, but they hit IndusInd harder than its peers (IL&FS shock −7%, Yes Bank crisis −10% versus peer banks): the market was already pricing its concentration risk. Year by year the link is weak: a 1-point rise in GNPA went with about 9 points of underperformance, but it explains only 7% of returns.

Adjusted prices rebased to 100 in April 2015 (log scale). Dotted lines mark the dated events tested below; red = bank-specific, blue = sector-wide or structural.

Event study: 3-day abnormal return

Bars show the return beyond what the overall market predicts, from the day before to the day after each event. Diamonds compare with peer banks instead. If both are strongly negative, the news was about this bank alone.

How to read it

There is a negative correlation (r = −0.27): years with rising bad loans tended to be worse years for the stock. It is weak because annual ratios arrive late, while the market prices news on the day it breaks. Correlation is not causation: other news (results, governance, the broader market) moves prices too.

04 · Data breaks

How we handled mergers and changing definitions

The brief asks for this explicitly. Each break is marked on the charts and kept out of the trend where it would mislead.

HDFC Ltd merger · FY2024

Added Rs 12,281 cr of bad loans and 55% more loans overnight.

Handled: merger additions excluded from slippages; charts show a break; pre- and post-merger read separately. No restated history exists.

BFIL into IndusInd · FY2020

Microfinance arm merged in July 2019 (Rs 50 cr of bad loans added).

Handled: excluded from slippages; flagged as a business-mix change.

Citibank India into Axis · FY2023

Rs 396 cr of bad loans came with the acquired retail business.

Handled: excluded from slippages; flagged.

RBI disclosure format · FY2022

RBI replaced the old "movement of NPAs" table with a new classification table.

Handled: mapped both formats to the same fields. Ratios reconcile within 0.05pp to every bank-reported figure we found.

Different PCR definitions

Kotak and Axis count written-off loans as "covered"; ICICI and IndusInd do not.

Handled: one Harmonised Implied PCR for all banks, (GNPA − NNPA) ÷ GNPA, excluding technical write-offs. It is a calculated proxy; bank-reported PCRs are stored separately.

Axis definition and restatements

Axis counts investments in its NPA ratio, moved to daily NPA tagging in FY2018, and restated some figures.

Handled: used the loans-only column; each year kept on its own report's basis; one typo in the FY2026 report corrected.

05 · Method & files

How it was built

Open any panel for detail. Everything here is downloadable.

Metric methodology notes

Harmonised Implied PCR = (GNPA − NNPA) ÷ GNPA × 100. A calculated proxy used to improve peer comparability. It excludes technical write-offs, so it is not the PCR each bank reports and can differ from it (Kotak and Axis, for example, include technical write-offs in their own PCR).

Specific NPA Credit Cost = specific NPA provisions charged to the P&L ÷ average net advances (opening and closing). Excluded: standard-asset provisions, COVID-related contingency provisions and floating provisions, so banks are compared on credit losses rather than discretionary buffers.

Event-study limitations

  • Event-study results are exploratory, not proof of causality.
  • Overlapping events and simultaneous announcements can influence abnormal returns (for example, March 2020 coincides with the COVID crash).
  • Accounting, governance and other non-credit events also move stock prices.
  • Testing many events raises the chance that some look significant by luck (false positives).
  • Statistical significance is not the same as economic or causal significance.
Data sources and checks

Credit-risk metrics: 50 audited annual reports (5 banks × 10 years) downloaded from BSE stock-exchange filings. Values come from the RBI-mandated bad-loan tables, the provisions note, the capital note and the balance sheet. Each figure carries its PDF page number.

Market data: daily share prices adjusted for splits, bonuses and dividends (Yahoo Finance), with the Nifty Bank and Nifty 50 indices, April 2015 to October 2026.

Checks: each bank's bad-loan movement (opening + new − upgrades − recoveries − write-offs = closing) adds up exactly for 42 of 50 bank-years. The 8 Axis gaps equal transfers Axis itself discloses. Our recalculated GNPA ratios match all 22 bank-reported ratios within 0.05pp, and the Excel workbook recalculates every figure with formulas.

Metric definitions
Event-study and correlation method

Abnormal return = actual return − expected return, where expected return comes from the bank's normal relationship with the Nifty 50 (a market model estimated over 250 trading days before each event). CAR adds abnormal returns from day −1 to day +1. Day 0 is the first trading day after the news. A t-statistic above about 2 in absolute value means the move is unusually large.

Peer-adjusted return = the bank's return minus the average return of its peers. It separates "the whole sector fell" from "this bank fell".

Correlation: yearly excess return over the Nifty 50 against the yearly change in GNPA %, pooled across all five banks (45 observations), with robust standard errors. This shows association, not causation.

Limitations
  • Annual audited data only; early-warning data (SMA-1/2, restructured loans) is not disclosed consistently, so it is marked unavailable rather than guessed.
  • No restated HDFC + HDFC Ltd history exists, so FY2024 is a hard break.
  • Specific NPA Credit Cost uses specific NPA provisions only; standard-asset, COVID-related contingency and floating provisions are excluded and logged.
  • Event studies cover one firm per event, and March 2020 events overlap with the COVID crash.
  • The regression has 45 observations, so it describes association only.
  • Both banks are category (a) large private banks; the brief's wording on picking "two of the options" should be confirmed.
